main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem} Suppose that a smooth almost complex structure J on a closed connected smooth real four-manifold X is tamed by a symplectic form. Then there is a smooth symplectic form compatible with J. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: On a closed connected 4-manifold, if some symplectic form omega satisfies omega(v,Jv)>0, then some (possibly different-class) symplectic form is J-invariant and positive on complex lines. Secondary: Thm 1.2 describes the compatible cone as the classes in C=K^t cap (H_J^-)^perp that pair strictly positively with closure(C); Cor 1.3: K^t=K^c+H_J^- when h_J^-=b^+-1 (so K^t=K^c if b^+=1).

comparator.theorem: OAI.TamingCompatibility.taming_implies_compatibility [T2Space X] [SecondCountableTopology X] [CompactSpace X] [ConnectedSpace X] (J : AlmostComplexStructure X) (h : ∃ α, IsSymplectic α ∧ Tames α J) : ∃ η, IsSymplectic η ∧ Compatible η J
comparator.model: X: ChartedSpace over EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4), IsManifold 𝓘 ∞ (C^∞). TwoForm = pointwise continuous alternating 2-maps on TangentSpace (no regularity built in). IsSmooth/IsClosed quantify over all C^∞ maps f from open U ⊆ ℝ^4 into X: pullback f*α is C^∞ and extDerivWithin of it vanishes on U. IsNondegenerate pointwise. Tames: ∀ x, v≠0 → 0 < α x ![v, J v]. IsInvariant: α(Ju,Jv)=α(u,v). Compatible = Tames ∧ IsInvariant. AlmostComplexStructure: J²=-1 and J is C^∞ as a map of the tangent bundle. definition_names = [] (definitions are in the challenge file; Model.lean is textually identical).

evidence.quote: Donaldson asked whether the existence of a taming symplectic form on a closed four-manifold implies the existence of a compatible one [Donaldson2006, Section 5.2, Question 2]. ... Our main result answers the existence question affirmatively.

primary_evidence.quote: If no compatible form exists, separation produces a nonzero positive current P that annihilates closed invariant forms. ... The resulting nonzero positive current P=T cannot annihilate a closed taming form.

D.max_item: I18 Thm 5.1 (closedness of the positive-density restriction for P+Q closed) together with I23 residual pairing; N2, N3-borderline

evidence.quote: Here only P+Q is initially closed, and the positive-density set is not assumed to be J-analytic; the mass and angular estimates provide the cutoff control needed for the restriction.

caveats: The overall architecture is a real-variable almost-complex transport of the Lamari/Buchdahl intersection argument on complex surfaces (boundary T with T.T=0; anti-invariant part self-dual so |Q|^2>=0) combined with Demailly-style regularization and a Siu-type split into positive-density and diffuse parts; this pushes the device toward N2.

Thm 5.1's hypothesis (only P+Q closed, Q in L^2 anti-invariant) is genuinely weaker than in El Mir-Skoda/Siu/Elkhadhra restriction theorems, and its proof (angular x transverse balance) has no neighbour found; a strict novelty pass could promote it to N3 (F3).
Lean proves the same splitting by a different mechanism (summable log activations + monotonicity-defect integrability), evidence that the statement is reachable by more than one route.
Grades conditional on correctness of an unrefereed, extraordinary claim; quick literature check only.

proof_architecture.claim: Separation: if no compatible form, a probability measure lambda on unit complex lines gives positive P killing closed invariant forms; closed lift B gives T=P+Q (Q=-P(BR.), anti-invariant, self-dual) killing all closed forms.
Quadratic mass growth mu(B_s)<=Cs^2 by testing P on closed invariant log/sqrt radial forms (1-BR)dd^c u.

Regularize by S_r=(1+r^2 Delta)^{-3}; kernel = positive transport part + error; angular identity turns <S_rP,*S_rP> into c r^{-4} I_r minus bounded shell error; mixing lemma bounds P.Q cross terms; zero pairing of T with itself yields Q in L^2, I_r<=Cr^4, and vanishing mixed limits.
Density theory: theta exists everywhere (Lelong-Jensen almost monotonicity); at positive-density points tangent currents are planar so the transverse moment N_r=o(r^2).

Thm 5.1: P_E=1_{theta>0}P is closed: smoothed density cutoff f_r; closure converts tangential derivatives into delta*|z^perp|/r, bounded by r^{-3}sqrt(I_r)sqrt(N_r)=o(1); Q-part by L^2 and theta=0 a.e.; then b_n(f) -> 1_E.

Residual pairing: T'=T-P_E closed; 0=<S_rT,*S_rT'>; negative error vanishes because P' sits on zero-density centers; mixed terms vanish; hence ||Q||^2<=0, Q=0, P=T kills the closed tamer omega, contradicting omega>0 on complex lines.

Cones (Sec 8, not formalized): prescribed-class separation, cohomological pairing, same estimates, residual pairing with arbitrary positive currents => Thm 1.2 and Cor 1.3; T^4 example of strict inclusion.

key_items_dag.hermitianMetric (DifferentialForms/Metri: used in 154 theorem signatures / 75 files; dependents 8.8%

route_differences_from_paper: Metric: Lean takes g = J-invariant part of the taming form alpha (hermitianMetric), normalizes P(alpha^inv)=1 and ends with <Q,alpha>=-1 contradicting Q=0 (Main.lean:46-50), instead of an arbitrary Hermitian metric and positivity of P(omega).

No density limit theta and no tangent measures: transverse decay comes from integrability of the radial 'defect' term (|z|^2|v|^2-<z,v>^2-<z,Jv>^2)/(s^2+|z|^2)^2 that the paper discards in Prop 3.1 (Concentration/RadialDefect.lean:39, RadialDefectCombination.lean:140, DifferentialForms/UnitTransverseLimit.lean). This is the Allard/Simon monotonicity-excess mechanism and gives decay at every centre.

Positive-density set E replaced by the exceptional set of summable logarithmic activations c_n = 2^-n log(1+f_n/delta_n) along chosen scales r_n (Charts/SlowLogCutoff.lean, Charts/SummableCutoff.lean, Concentration/ActivationScales.lean, ConcentrationActivations.lean); restriction to it is closed by restriction_zero_of_tail_bounds.

Q is obtained directly as a weak L^2 limit of regularized corrections (weak_limit_functional_represented in separating_current_L2_correction), not first in H^{-3}; the closed lift is built from a convergent regularized family on an atlas, apparently without a PsiDO calculus (text-level reading).
Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3 and Example 8.6 are not formalized.

eureka_candidates.for: Authors' 'principal step'; it is what makes T'=T-P_E closed and hence the residual pairing possible. Hypothesis is strictly weaker than any restriction theorem found (P itself is not closed); the balance r^{-3}·O(r^2)·o(r)=o(1) pairing the angular moment with the transverse moment has no neighbour found. Reused verbatim by companion family 341 (Donaldson's hypersymplectic conjecture), i.e. a device reused for a second problem.
eureka_candidates.against: The conclusion has the same shape as El Mir-Skoda / Siu-decomposition / Elkhadhra 2014 restriction results for closed positive currents (cited by the paper). Ingredients are classical: Lelong-type monotonicity, tangent measures/constancy theorem, smoothed density cutoffs. The Lean reaches the same split by a different, also classical route (summable log cutoffs + monotonicity excess), so the statement is reachable in more than one way. 341 is the same model's companion on a neighbouring Donaldson question, so the reuse is weak evidence.

correctness_audit.verdict: Extraordinary claim: resolves Donaldson's 2006 tamed-to-compatible question for all closed 4-manifolds (previous results needed b^+=1 or h_J^-=b^+-1, and TWZZ2022's b^+=1 argument was questioned by Lin-Zhou 2025). Paper is short (~1.6k lines of mathematics) and internally coherent at the level read; I found no gap in a line-by-line read of Secs 2-7. Trust rests mainly on the Lean: 83k lines, text-level clean (no sorry/axiom/native_decide/set_option), comparator statement faithful. Compile result pending from orchestrator; if it builds with only the 3 permitted axioms, Thm 1.1 is machine-checked.
